title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v126
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds profiling baselines and a reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab v126. Improvements to runner stability, new telemetry tags, and updated dashboards.
description: Motivation: this PR adds profiling baselines and a reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab (v126). The goal is to capture representative workload profiles, provide stable baseline traces for kernel-selection experiments, and feed aggregated metrics into the reporting pipeline so data scientists and infra can track regressions. Scope: - Add new workload runners for memory- and kernel-focused profiles - Persist profiling baselines to benchmark-store with versioning tags - Add a reporting pipeline job (Airflow DAG + export scripts) that aggregates latency/p95, p99, memory snapshots, and kernel-selection histograms - Add telemetry tags to existing runners to correlate by sequence-length and batch-config - Update dashboards and alerting queries Checklist: - [x] Implement representative workload runners - [x] Add baseline storage and versioning schema - [x] Add reporting DAG and exporter script - [x] Update Grafana dashboard queries - [x] Add CI smoke tests for new runners Implementation notes: commits include small, focused changes: new runner modules in benchmark-lab/runners/, a baseline persister under benchmark-lab/store/, an airflow DAG under telemetry/dags/benchmark_reporting_v126.py, and a reporting exporter script telemetry/exporters/report_aggregator_v126.py. The reporting pipeline writes daily aggregated CSVs and pushes metrics to metrics-ingest. This PR intentionally avoids changing the main serving runtime; it only augments the lab tooling and reporting. Related: ENG-1429 (baseline schema), ENG-1430 (reporting pipeline). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1429/benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines. CI notes: initially flaky due to a race in runner startup; fixed by adding a runner initialization backoff and health check. All CI checks passed on the final run. Merge strategy: squash and merge after approval.
commits: feat(benchmark-lab): add memory and kernel profiling workload runners
feat(store): baseline persister with versioned keys and TTL
feat(telemetry): add reporting DAG for daily aggregates (v126)
chore(ci): add smoke test for benchmark-lab runners
fix(runners): add startup backoff and readiness probe to avoid CI race
diff_snippets: +++ benchmark-lab/runners/memory_runner.py: add MemoryRunner class with run_profile() that records rss/vms at checkpoints
+++ telemetry/dags/benchmark_reporting_v126.py: Airflow DAG with daily schedule, tasks: pull_baselines -> aggregate_metrics -> push_metrics
+++ telemetry/exporters/report_aggregator_v126.py: aggregator reads baseline store and runner outputs, emits CSV and metrics via metrics-sdk
